title: 01. Foundations: Tokenization
summary: Tokenization is the process of breaking text into smaller pieces called "tokens" that the LLM can process.

sections.title: 5.1 What is Tokenization?
sections.body:
### Simple Definition
> **Tokenization is the process of breaking text into smaller pieces called "tokens" that the LLM can process.**

Computers don't understand text — they understand numbers. So we must convert text → tokens → numbers.

### Analogy: LEGO Bricks
> Think of text as a LEGO creation. Tokenization breaks it into individual LEGO bricks (tokens). The LLM works with these bricks, then assembles them back into a creation (response).

### How Tokenization Works

```
Original text: "Hello, I love Generative AI!"

WORD-LEVEL tokenization (old way):
["Hello", ",", "I", "love", "Generative", "AI", "!"]
                                     ↑
                          What if "Generative" isn't in vocabulary?
                          
SUBWORD tokenization (modern way - BPE):
["Hello", ",", "▁I", "▁love", "▁Gen", "erative", "▁AI", "!"]
                               ↑
                 Common words stay whole, rare words are split
```

### Real Example with GPT Tokenizer
```
Text: "Tokenization is fascinating!"
Tokens: ["Token", "ization", " is", " fasci", "nating", "!"]
IDs:    [  9159,   1634,     374,   37580,    1112,    0  ]
```

### Key Facts About Tokens
- **1 token ≈ 4 characters** or **¾ of a word** (in English)
- "ChatGPT" = 1 token
- "Generative" = 2 tokens ["Gen", "erative"]
- 1000 words ≈ 750 tokens
- Different languages tokenize differently (English is most efficient)

### Why Tokenization Matters
```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  WHY TOKENIZATION MATTERS                            │
│                                                      │
│  1. COST: APIs charge per token                      │
│     → Fewer tokens = cheaper!                        │
│                                                      │
│  2. CONTEXT LIMIT: Models have max token limits      │
│     → Can't process unlimited text                   │
│                                                      │
│  3. PERFORMANCE: Some words split into many tokens   │
│     → Can affect reasoning on special terms          │
│                                                      │
│  4. LANGUAGES: Non-English text uses more tokens     │
│     → Same content costs more in other languages     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: 5.2 Types of Tokenizers
sections.body:
| Tokenizer | How It Works | Used By |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| **BPE** (Byte Pair Encoding) | Merges frequent character pairs | GPT-2, GPT-3, GPT-4 |
| **WordPiece** | Similar to BPE, different merging | BERT, Google models |
| **SentencePiece** | Works at byte level, language agnostic | Llama, T5 |
| **Tiktoken** | OpenAI's fast tokenizer | GPT-4, ChatGPT |
